Guidance: Tasks that shell out to raw commands (command/shell modules) without changed_when report 'changed' every run, breaking idempotency checks and making --check unreliable.
Do: Prefer purpose-built modules over shell/command, and set changed_when/creates for unavoidable shell tasks.
Don't: Use shell: to run arbitrary commands with no changed_when guard.
Example: - name: check disk\n  command: df -h\n  changed_when: false

Guidance: Committing plaintext passwords or API keys into group_vars is a common source of leaked secrets when a repo goes from private to public or an old commit is scraped.
Do: Encrypt all secret-bearing variable files with ansible-vault and keep the vault password out of version control.
Don't: Store plaintext credentials in group_vars/all.yml committed to git.

Keywords: inventory, dynamic inventory, inventory plugin, static hosts
Guidance: Static INI inventories drift from reality in cloud environments where instances come and go; a dynamic inventory plugin (aws_ec2, azure_rm) queries the actual current state.
Do: Use a dynamic inventory plugin for cloud-hosted fleets so inventory always reflects live infrastructure.
Don't: Maintain a hand-edited static inventory file for an autoscaled cloud fleet.

Keywords: handler, notify, service restart, task ordering
Guidance: Restarting a service unconditionally in every task run wastes time and can cause unnecessary downtime; handlers only fire when a notifying task actually reports 'changed'.
Do: Use notify + handlers for actions (like service restarts) that should only happen when a preceding task changed something.
Don't: Put an unconditional service restart task after every config file edit.
Example: handlers:\n  - name: restart nginx\n    service: {name: nginx, state: restarted}

Keywords: ansible role, galaxy, role structure, reusable playbook
Guidance: Copy-pasting the same task blocks across multiple playbooks means a fix has to be applied in every copy; roles package reusable, testable units of automation.
Do: Extract common functionality into roles with clear defaults/vars, and version them (Galaxy or a git tag) for reuse across playbooks.
Don't: Duplicate the same 40-line task block across five different playbooks.

Topic: Check mode and diff before apply
Guidance: Running a new or edited playbook directly against production without --check first risks an untested task making an unintended change at scale, across every host in the play simultaneously.
Do: Run ansible-playbook --check --diff against a subset of hosts before a full production run.
Don't: Run a newly written playbook directly against the full production inventory.

Guidance: Setting become: true at the play level when only one task actually needs root grants every task in that play elevated privileges unnecessarily.
Do: Scope become to the specific tasks that need elevated privileges rather than the whole play.
Don't: Set become: true globally at the play level 'just in case'.
Example: - name: install package\n  apt: {name: nginx, state: present}\n  become: true

Guidance: Without tags, testing a single change in a large playbook means running the entire play end to end, slowing iteration and increasing blast radius of a test run.
Do: Tag logical sections (config, packages, deploy) so specific parts of a playbook can be run or skipped independently.
Don't: Run the full playbook top to bottom to test a one-line config change.

Keywords: jinja2, undefined variable, default filter, templating
Guidance: Referencing an undefined variable inside a Jinja2 template fails the whole task with a cryptic error at runtime instead of failing fast with a clear message.
Do: Use the default() filter or explicit variable validation (assert) for optional variables referenced in templates.
Don't: Reference optional variables in templates with no default filter and no upstream validation.

Keywords: fact caching, gather_facts, setup module, performance
Guidance: Re-gathering facts from every host on every playbook run adds significant wall-clock time to large inventories when facts rarely change between runs.
Do: Enable fact caching (e.g. to Redis or JSON files) with a sensible TTL for large inventories run frequently.
Don't: Leave fact caching disabled on a 500-host inventory run every few minutes.

Guidance: Without block/rescue, a single failed task in a multi-step playbook aborts the whole play on that host with no cleanup, potentially leaving a host in a half-configured state.
Do: Wrap risky multi-step operations in block/rescue/always so failures can be handled and cleanup always runs.
Don't: Let a mid-playbook failure abort with no rescue block, leaving partial state on the host.
Example:
block:
  - name: risky task
    command: /opt/deploy.sh
rescue:
  - name: rollback
    command: /opt/rollback.sh

Guidance: Ansible's variable precedence order (role defaults < inventory group_vars < host_vars < play vars < extra-vars) surprises users when a value doesn't override what they expect -- extra-vars always wins.
Do: Understand and document the precedence order in use, and prefer group_vars/host_vars over scattered play-level vars for anything environment-specific.
Don't: Set the same variable in five different precedence layers and guess which one wins.

Keywords: molecule, role testing, ci for ansible
Guidance: Roles changed without automated testing regress silently -- a working role today can break next month's Ansible or collection upgrade with no test to catch it.
Do: Write Molecule scenarios (with a Docker/Vagrant driver) to test roles in CI on every change.
Don't: Ship and update roles with zero automated test coverage.
